title: Engineering activity dashboard
request: create an engineering activity dashboard based on these tables
desire: Engineering leads want one dashboard showing how much work the team is doing and how it flows over the last 90 days, by week: pull requests opened, merged and still open plus median time to merge; commits and active committers; code review comments, reviewers and reviewed PRs; issues opened, closed and still open. Only people count: bot accounts are excluded. It rests on the raw GitHub extract in the github database (raw.pull_requests, raw.commits, raw.pull_request_review_comments, raw.issues), cleaned in staging, modelled as one fact per activity in marts, published to the Library with measures and segments, and read by the dashboard's cards only through those definitions.

outcomes.title: An Engineering activity dashboard
outcomes.description: Weekly PR flow, commits, code review and issues for the last 90 days, human activity only, built on new staging, marts and semantic definitions over the raw GitHub tables.

architecture.title: Layers and schemas
architecture.decision: Staging transforms write schema staging, fact transforms write schema marts, both in the github Database; raw stays untouched.
architecture.rationale: There are no guides yet, so this follows the usual raw, staging, marts split and keeps outputs out of the raw source schema.

architecture.title: Fact grains
architecture.decision: fct_pull_requests has one row per PR number, fct_commits one per commit sha, fct_pr_review_comments one per review comment id, fct_issues one per issue number excluding PRs.
architecture.rationale: Probes show each key is unique in raw, and every dashboard question is a count or median over one of these activities.

architecture.title: Bot rule
architecture.decision: is_bot is derived once in staging (user_type = 'Bot' or login ending in '[bot]'; commits by login only) and excluded through a Human segment per fact on every card.
architecture.rationale: Keeps bot rows available for later analysis while every dashboard number counts people only, as the user chose.

architecture.title: Issues exclude pull requests
architecture.decision: stg_issues keeps only rows where is_pull_request is false.
architecture.rationale: GitHub lists PRs in the issues endpoint; 14,033 of the 15,971 raw issue rows are PRs already covered by raw.pull_requests.

architecture.title: Window in cards, no dashboard filter
architecture.decision: Each card filters its own date column to the previous 90 days with weekly breakouts; backlog cards show current open counts with no window.
architecture.rationale: Cards use different date columns (created, merged, authored, closed), so one dashboard date filter would be misleading; commits and review comments only exist from Aug 2026.

architecture.title: Refresh
architecture.decision: All eight transforms carry one tag run by a daily transform job.
architecture.rationale: Production keeps the dashboard current after merge without manual runs.

changes.title: Add staging transforms for pull requests, commits, review comments and issues, with a daily job
changes.justification: Marts must not read raw, so each raw table gets one staging transform that renames, types and derives is_bot once (architecture: Bot rule; Layers and schemas). No guides exist yet.
checks: stg_pull_requests has 14,031 rows, unique on pull_request_number; 231 have is_bot true
stg_commits has 2,445 rows, unique on commit_sha; 105 have is_bot true
stg_pr_review_comments has 9,023 rows, unique on review_comment_id; every pull_request_number parses (0 nulls); 231 have is_bot true
stg_issues has 1,938 rows (PRs excluded), unique on issue_number; 125 have is_bot true
no transform uses SELECT *

approach.do: stg_pull_requests: read raw.pull_requests, one row per number; rename number to pull_request_number, user_login to author_login, draft to is_draft; keep state, base_ref, created_at, closed_at, merged_at
stg_pull_requests: derive is_merged = merged_at not null; is_bot = user_type = 'Bot' or user_login ends with '[bot]'; write staging.stg_pull_requests

stg_commits: read raw.commits, one row per sha as commit_sha; author_login, author_date as authored_at, committer_login, verified as is_verified; is_bot = author_login ends with '[bot]'; write staging.stg_commits

stg_pr_review_comments: read raw.pull_request_review_comments, one row per id as review_comment_id; parse pull_request_number from pull_request_url after '/pulls/'; user_login as reviewer_login; pull_request_review_id as review_id; created_at
stg_pr_review_comments: derive is_reply = in_reply_to_id not null; is_bot by the user_type/login rule; write staging.stg_pr_review_comments

stg_issues: read raw.issues where is_pull_request is false, one row per number as issue_number; title, state, state_reason, user_login as author_login, created_at, closed_at; is_bot by the rule; write staging.stg_issues
add transform collection Staging (namespace transforms), tag github_activity on all transforms, and job GitHub activity daily at 06:00 running that tag

changes.title: Add activity facts: fct_pull_requests, fct_commits, fct_pr_review_comments, fct_issues
changes.justification: One fact per activity at the grain each dashboard question counts (architecture: Fact grains), reading staging only (architecture: Layers and schemas).
checks: fct_pull_requests: 14,031 rows, unique pull_request_number; hours_to_merge is null exactly when merged_at is null and never negative
fct_commits: 2,445 rows, unique commit_sha
fct_pr_review_comments: 9,023 rows, unique review_comment_id; every pull_request_number exists in fct_pull_requests (0 orphans in raw)
fct_issues: 1,938 rows, unique issue_number; hours_to_close null when closed_at is null

planning-time human values over the previous 90 days: 5,727 PRs opened, 4,584 merged, median 21.47 hours to merge, 582 open PRs; 2,312 commits; 8,681 review comments; 761 issues opened, 1,204 open (these move with time)

approach.do: fct_pull_requests: read staging.stg_pull_requests at grain pull_request_number; derive is_open = state 'open', hours_to_merge = (merged_at - created_at) in hours; write marts.fct_pull_requests
fct_commits: read staging.stg_commits at grain commit_sha, columns carried as they are; write marts.fct_commits

fct_pr_review_comments: read staging.stg_pr_review_comments at grain review_comment_id; left join staging.stg_pull_requests on pull_request_number for pr_author_login; write marts.fct_pr_review_comments
fct_issues: read staging.stg_issues at grain issue_number; derive is_open = state 'open', hours_to_close = (closed_at - created_at) in hours; write marts.fct_issues
add transform collection Marts (namespace transforms); tag every fact github_activity so the daily job runs it after staging

changes.title: Publish the four activity facts to the Library with their keys
changes.justification: Cards read only Library definitions; publishing the facts with key fields makes their measures and segments available and declares the review comment to PR link (architecture: Fact grains).
checks: the four tables are published in the Library Data collection with display names Pull requests, Commits, PR review comments, Issues
each table description states its grain and that is_bot marks bot accounts
fct_pr_review_comments.pull_request_number is a foreign key to fct_pull_requests.pull_request_number

approach.do: add the github Database file and the Library, Data and Metrics collection files exactly as Metabase defines them
publish marts.fct_pull_requests as Pull requests (one row per PR), key pull_request_number (PK)
publish marts.fct_commits as Commits (one row per commit), key commit_sha (PK)
publish marts.fct_pr_review_comments as PR review comments (one row per comment), review_comment_id PK, pull_request_number FK to fct_pull_requests
publish marts.fct_issues as Issues (one row per issue, PRs excluded), key issue_number (PK)

changes.title: Add activity measures and segments, including Human segments that exclude bots
changes.justification: Every dashboard number is defined once in the Library and reused; the Human segments carry the bot exclusion the user chose (architecture: Bot rule).
checks: PR count over Human PRs = 13,800 (14,031 minus 231 bot PRs); with Open PRs = 582 at planning time
Commit count over Human commits = 2,340 (2,445 minus 105 bot commits)
Review comment count over Human review comments = 8,792 (9,023 minus 231)
Issue count over Human issues = 1,813 (1,938 minus 125); with Open issues = 1,204 at planning time
every measure and segment has a description stating its rule

approach.do: Pull requests: measure PR count = count of rows; measure Median hours to merge = median of hours_to_merge; segments Human PRs = is_bot false, Merged PRs = is_merged true, Open PRs = is_open true
Commits: measure Commit count = count of rows; measure Active committers = distinct author_login; segment Human commits = is_bot false
PR review comments: measures Review comment count = count, Active reviewers = distinct reviewer_login, Reviewed PRs = distinct pull_request_number; segment Human review comments = is_bot false
Issues: measure Issue count = count of rows; segments Human issues = is_bot false, Open issues = is_open true, Closed issues = closed_at not null

changes.title: Add the Engineering activity dashboard
changes.justification: The requested artifact; every card reads a Library measure with its Human segment, previous 90 days by week (architecture: Window in cards, no dashboard filter; Bot rule).
checks: every card returns rows on the branch and aggregates a Library measure (no native SQL, no staging or raw table)
every card applies its table's Human segment
scalars at planning time: PRs opened 5,727, PRs merged 4,584, median hours to merge 21.47, open PRs 582, open issues 1,204 (they move with time)
dashboard has four sections: Pull request flow, Commits, Code review, Issues

approach.do: PR KPIs, previous 90 days, Human PRs: PRs opened = PR count by created_at; PRs merged = PR count + Merged PRs by merged_at; Median hours to merge = measure + Merged PRs by merged_at; Open PRs = PR count + Open PRs, no window
PR trends: PRs opened per week = PR count by week of created_at; PRs merged per week = PR count + Merged PRs by week of merged_at; both Human PRs, previous 90 days, line charts

Commits, Human commits, previous 90 days by authored_at: Commits per week = Commit count by week (bar); Active committers per week = Active committers by week (line); Top committers = Commit count by author_login, top 10 (row)

Code review, Human review comments, previous 90 days by created_at: Review comments per week (bar); Reviewed PRs per week = Reviewed PRs and Active reviewers by week (line); Top reviewers = Review comment count by reviewer_login, top 10 (row)

Issues, Human issues, previous 90 days: Issues opened per week = Issue count by week of created_at; Issues closed per week = Issue count + Closed issues by week of closed_at; Open issues = Issue count + Open issues, no window

dashboard Engineering activity in collection Engineering: heading per section, KPI scalars on top, trends then top-10 tables; description notes bots are excluded and commits/review data start Aug 2026
